_why: cross-channel-overlay: the plot opens stacked as before; the view switch is there, and the stack's own y and align controls stay

cross-channel-overlay: ?view=overlay draws one path per channel of the recording in one tall block (data-height >= 420, data-lane >= 28, data-channels = the channel count); the y and align controls of the stack hide, the overlay's own header carries align by lag, all / none and box the span
cross-channel-overlay: a plain click on a name makes that channel the only bold one and fades the rest (data-bold on the name and the path); the address remembers it as ?bold=

cross-channel-overlay: align by lag shifts each channel by its measured lag against the reference: the overlay says data-align=lag, every non-reference name prints its shift (data-shift), and at least one channel's group carries a non-zero data-shift. If the last fails on real data, read the shifts: every lag 0 or past ±60 s is a finding, not a drawing fault (the same caveat as aq-lag-aligned-moves-rows)

cross-channel-overlay: a box across the overlay (here 'box the span', the same state a drag sets) shows the shared action strip under it — Zoom, Send unjudged, Mark artifact, Open in Analyse, Open in Signal — with a caption naming the box and the bold channels. Nothing is clicked in the strip, so nothing is written
